purpose: A contract fragment adding one layer, merged into `model-contract.json` IN THE TEST PROCESS ONLY (`model_contract_fixtures.merged_contract`). Nothing production-side loads it, no fixture project on disk gains a `synthetic/` directory, and the shipped contract is not rewritten. The layer is deliberately unremarkable — a `name` identity, a flat storage record, `arxmlBound: false`, a declared `token`, one ordinary scalar field and one reference to an existing layer — because what it has to demonstrate is that a layer nobody wrote special handling for is still accounted for everywhere. A fixture with an interesting shape would prove only that the interesting shape was handled. The completeness checker reports its missing dispositions deterministically and NAMES them. The layer declares its `token` rather than exercising the fallback, for the same reason it answers `arxmlBound`: this fragment stands in for a layer someone would really add, and a real layer declares what the shipped layers declare. Its name happens to be its own token, so the value is unremarkable too; the case that a token is NOT derivable from the name — a layer named `taxes` whose token is `tax` — is exercised in the test process by `packages/tools/tests/test_impact.py`, where a wrong token is visible in the output.
